st: Rub the chicken all over with salt and rinse it, then pat dry. Put [[2 tbsp]] sliced ginger and the scallions inside the cavity.
Bring a pot of water big enough to cover the chicken to a boil, then lower the chicken in and turn the heat off. Cover and let it sit for 45 minutes.
Check that the thickest part of the thigh reads 165°F (74°C). If not, return it to hot water for 10 more minutes.
Move the chicken to a bowl of ice water for 10 minutes so the skin turns smooth and firm, then drain and rub it with [[1 tbsp]] sesame oil.
Rinse the rice until the water runs clear, then drain well.
Heat [[2 tbsp]] vegetable oil in a pot, add [[4 clove]] chopped garlic and [[1 tbsp]] ginger and fry for 1 minute. Stir in the rice for 2 minutes.
Add [[3 cup]] chicken broth and a pinch of salt, bring to a boil, cover, and cook on low for 18 minutes. Rest 10 minutes off the heat.
Blend the chili, [[2 clove]] garlic, [[2 tbsp]] cooking broth, [[1 tbsp]] rice vinegar, [[1 tsp]] sugar and a pinch of salt into a rough sauce.
Chop the chicken into pieces. Serve over the rice with cucumber, the chili sauce, and [[2 tbsp]] soy sauce for dipping.

ing: cleaned and cut into pieces; or 2 lb crab legs
st: Crack the crab claws lightly with the back of a knife so the sauce can get in.
Heat [[3 tbsp]] oil in a large wok over medium heat. Fry the garlic, ginger and chili for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in [[3 tbsp]] tomato paste, [[0.25 cup]] ketchup and [[2 tbsp]] chili sauce and cook for 2 minutes.
Add [[1 cup]] water, [[2 tbsp]] sugar and a pinch of salt and bring to a simmer.
Add the crab, cover and cook for 12 minutes, turning once, until the shells are bright red and the meat is opaque.
Stir the cornstarch mix and pour it in, cooking 1 minute until the sauce thickens.
Turn off the heat. Slowly drizzle in the eggs while stirring to form ribbons.
Top with scallions and serve with bread or steamed rice for the sauce.
Boil the eggs for 10 minutes, cool in cold water, then peel and halve them.
Blend the chili, lemongrass, shallots, garlic, ginger, turmeric and shrimp paste with a splash of water into a paste.
Heat [[3 tbsp]] oil in a pot and fry the paste on medium heat for 6 minutes until darker and fragrant.
Pour in [[3 cup]] broth and the coconut milk. Simmer gently for 15 minutes and season with salt.
Cook the noodles as the package says, drain and rinse under cool water.
Add the shrimp and fish cake to the soup and cook 3 minutes until the shrimp are pink.
Divide the noodles and bean sprouts among bowls and ladle the hot soup over.
Top with egg halves and serve with lime wedges.

ing: or extra soy sauce plus 1 tsp sugar
st: If using dried noodles, soak them in warm water until soft, then drain. Separate fresh noodles gently.
Mix [[1 tbsp]] soy sauce, [[1 tbsp]] dark soy sauce, [[1 tsp]] chili paste and [[0.25 tsp]] white pepper in a small bowl.
Heat a wok on high heat until very hot. Add [[1 tbsp]] oil and fry the sausage for 1 minute.
Add [[2 tbsp]] oil and the garlic, then the shrimp. Stir-fry for 1 minute until the shrimp start to turn pink.
Add the noodles and sauce. Toss quickly for 2 minutes so they pick up color and a little char.
Push the noodles to one side, crack in the eggs, and scramble them for 30 seconds.
Add the bean sprouts and chives and toss for 1 minute. The sprouts should stay crisp.
Serve right away while hot.

ing: shells and heads saved if possible
st: Peel the shrimp and keep the shells. Simmer the shells in [[5 cup]] water with the pork belly for 25 minutes to make a stock.
Strain the stock into a bowl, discarding the shells. Slice the pork and keep it.
Soak the vermicelli in hot water for 5 minutes, then drain. Rinse the egg noodles in hot water and drain.
Heat [[3 tbsp]] oil in a wok on high heat. Fry the garlic for 20 seconds, then add the eggs and scramble loosely.
Add both noodles, [[1 tbsp]] soy sauce and [[1 tbsp]] fish sauce. Toss for 2 minutes.
Pour in [[2 cup]] of the stock, cover, and cook 4 minutes until the noodles absorb most of it.
Add shrimp, squid, pork and a bit more stock. Cook uncovered 3 minutes until the shrimp are pink and the squid is opaque.
Add bean sprouts and chives, toss for 1 minute, and serve with lime wedges.
Put the ribs in a pot, cover with water, and boil for 5 minutes. Drain and rinse off the foam.
Bring [[8 cup]] fresh water to a boil in the clean pot.
Add the ribs, garlic heads, [[2 tbsp]] crushed pepper, star anise, cinnamon and cloves.
Reduce to a low simmer, partly covered, and cook for 90 minutes.
Add [[2 tbsp]] soy sauce, [[1 tbsp]] dark soy sauce and [[1 tsp]] salt. Simmer another 30 minutes until the pork is very tender.
While the soup cooks, rinse the rice and cook it with [[3 cup]] water until fluffy.
Check that the pork is at least 145°F (63°C). Taste the broth and add salt if needed.
Serve the ribs and broth in bowls with rice alongside.

ing: snapper or salmon head, cleaned and halved; or 1.5 lb fish steaks
st: Mix [[3 tbsp]] curry powder with a little water to make a loose paste.
Heat [[3 tbsp]] oil in a pot and cook the onion for 5 minutes until soft.
Add garlic, ginger and the curry paste, and fry for 2 minutes.
Pour in [[2 cup]] water, the coconut milk, [[2 tbsp]] tamarind paste and [[1 tsp]] salt. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Add the eggplant and chilies and simmer for 8 minutes.
Lay the fish head in the pot and simmer, covered, for 10 minutes without stirring hard.
Add the okra and tomatoes and cook 6 more minutes until the fish is opaque and flakes.
Taste for salt and sourness and serve hot with rice.
Blend half the shallots, [[1 clove]] garlic, the lemongrass, turmeric, coriander, [[2 tbsp]] soy sauce, [[1 tbsp]] sugar and [[1 tbsp]] oil into a paste.
Toss the chicken with the paste and marinate in the fridge for 30 minutes.
Blend the peanuts, remaining shallots, [[2 clove]] garlic and the chilies into a coarse paste.
Heat [[2 tbsp]] oil in a pan and cook the peanut paste for 4 minutes, stirring.
Add [[0.75 cup]] water, [[2 tbsp]] sugar and [[1 tbsp]] tamarind paste. Simmer 8 minutes until thick, then add salt.
Thread the chicken onto skewers.
Grill or broil on high for 4 minutes per side until browned and 165°F (74°C) inside.
Serve with the peanut sauce and sliced cucumber.
Rinse the rice until the water runs clear and drain. Put it in a pot with [[1 cup]] coconut milk, [[1 cup]] water, pandan and [[1 tsp]] salt.
Bring to a boil, cover, and cook on low for 18 minutes. Let it rest 10 minutes.
Boil the eggs for 10 minutes, cool, and peel.
Fry the anchovies in [[0.5 cup]] hot oil for 2 minutes until crisp. Drain them on paper towels. Fry the peanuts in the same oil for 1 minute and drain.
Blend the chilies, shallots and garlic into a paste.
In a pan with [[2 tbsp]] of the frying oil, cook the paste for 8 minutes until it darkens and the oil separates.
Stir in [[1 tbsp]] sugar, [[1 tsp]] tamarind paste and salt to taste for the sambal.
Plate rice with sambal, eggs, cucumber, anchovies and peanuts.
Simmer the grated radish with [[1 cup]] water for 10 minutes until soft. Do not drain.
Whisk [[1.5 cup]] rice flour, [[1 cup]] water, [[1 tsp]] salt and [[0.5 tsp]] white pepper until smooth.
Stir the batter into the radish and cook on low for 5 minutes, stirring, until very thick.
Pour into an oiled 8-inch pan, smooth the top, and steam for 45 minutes.
Cool completely, about 1 hour, then cut into 1-inch cubes.
Heat [[3 tbsp]] oil in a wok and fry the cubes until golden, 5 minutes.
Add the garlic and preserved radish, then pour in the beaten eggs. Let them set for 30 seconds, then toss.
Season with [[2 tbsp]] soy sauce and [[1 tbsp]] sweet soy sauce, add scallions, and serve.
Mix the flour, [[1 tbsp]] sugar and [[1 tsp]] salt in a bowl. Add the egg, [[0.5 cup]] warm milk, [[0.5 cup]] water and [[2 tbsp]] melted butter.
Knead for 8 minutes into a soft smooth dough.
Divide into 8 balls and coat each in oil. Cover and rest for 1 hour.
Oil your work surface. Flatten one ball and stretch it very thin by pulling gently from the edges.
Fold the thin dough into a rope, then coil it into a spiral. Tuck the end under. Repeat with each ball and rest 10 minutes.
Flatten each spiral into a thick round.
Heat a griddle over medium heat with a bit of butter. Cook each round 2 minutes per side until golden.
Crush each prata with both hands to fluff the layers. Serve with warm curry.
Whisk 3 eggs and [[0.5 cup]] sugar in a heatproof bowl until combined.
Stir in [[0.75 cup]] coconut milk and add the pandan leaves.
Set the bowl over a pot of barely simmering water. Stir constantly for 30 minutes until thick like pudding.
Discard the pandan and let the kaya cool. It thickens more as it cools.
Boil 2 more eggs in simmering water for 6 minutes, cool briefly, and crack into a small dish.
Toast the bread until golden and crisp.
Spread kaya on 2 slices and add slices of cold butter, about [[3 tbsp]] in all.
Top with the other slices. Serve with the soft eggs, a few drops of soy sauce, and pepper.
Soak the mushrooms in hot water for 30 minutes, then squeeze dry and slice. Save the soaking water for the stock.
Heat [[1 tbsp]] oil in a pan over medium-high heat. Cook the garlic for 30 seconds, then add the pork and break it up. Cook 6 minutes until no pink remains.
Add the mushrooms, [[1 tbsp]] soy sauce and sugar to the pork and cook 2 minutes. Keep warm.
Heat the stock with the mushroom water and simmer for 10 minutes to make a light soup.
Mix [[2 tbsp]] oil, [[2 tbsp]] soy sauce, the black vinegar, sesame oil and chili sauce in a large bowl to make the dressing.
Boil the noodles in plenty of water for 2 minutes until springy, drain well, and toss in the dressing.
Top with the pork and mushrooms, fried shallots and scallions. Serve with the hot soup on the side.
nt: Pork stir-fried, noodles boiled and tossed in vinegar
Best swap: use balsamic vinegar with a pinch of sugar if you cannot find black vinegar; ground chicken works for pork.
